newsitem.title: UK: Protestors removed from UK airport.
newsitem.headline: Protestors removed from UK airport.

text.p: Environmental protesters were evicted on Tuesday from their network of tunnels and tree houses around a new runway at Manchester airport, northern England.
Bailiffs backed by police moved onto the land where the second runway is being built at the northern English airport.
The 100 demonstrators who had been served a writ last week vowed to keep their protest going at the 172 million pound runway development.
One of the protesters, named only as Phil, said after being evicted from his tunnel that he was sprayed with riot gas.
Vowing to fight on, he told BBC Radio: "They have only hit two of our five camps. To get people out of the big tunnels could take a couple of weeks."
But Manchester Airport Authority chairman and local member of parliament Graham Stringer said: "They are very incompetent protesters. They do not have the support of the local community."
